errors.english: These phenomena are not without afflictions
errors.why: The Tibetan says these dharmas are without afflictions (and are not afflicted), which the following 'why?' clause then justifies; the English negates the first member.

note: A sound rendering of the Akṣayamati citation and the argument on non-arising; one likely negation slip.
Faithful word-by-word gloss commentary on the tigress episode; only cosmetic problems in the transliterated lemmas.

errors.english: One should not accept (Apoha) exclusion of others as the primary object of sound, because this would be a denial
errors.why: The ཞེ་ན marks this as the opponent's objection (exclusion should not be accepted as word-meaning because a cognition refutes it), not the author's assertion.

fix.find: One should not accept (Apoha) exclusion of others as the primary object of sound, because this would be a denial
fix.replace: Objection: one should not accept (Apoha) exclusion of others as the meaning of a word, because [a cognition] refutes it

errors.why: གཞལ་བྱ is prameya (the cognizable/object of valid cognition), not jñeya (ཤེས་བྱ).

errors.english: how does the cognition arise which refutes the meaning of sound as (Apoha) exclusion from sounds other than that?
errors.why: The question is how a cognition refuting exclusion as word-meaning arises FROM words etc. that do not express other-exclusion; the English attaches 'from' to 'exclusion'.

errors.english: refers to things other than (Apoha), such as the sounds themselves
errors.why: 'That' refers to [the cognition from] words etc. that do not express exclusion, not to 'things other than apoha, such as the sounds'.

note: Readable but the dialectic is blurred: the opening objection is given as the author's view and the prameya term is mislabelled.
Accurate rendering of the argument against shape-distinctions in partless atoms and on conventional existence of the vase.
Careful and faithful, with root-text lemmas and the cetanā/cetayitvā distinction correctly handled.

errors.english: has been felled in its prime
errors.why: ཉམ་ངར (rendering Skt. kaṣṭam) is 'alas, painfully'; nothing in the Tibetan says 'in its prime'.

note: Good parallel rendering of the Sanskrit and Tibetan verses; one small embellishment.

errors.english:
Even if any particular condition of the wind humor or others were the cause, not every specific instance would possess all forms of desire and so forth. One must infer this because a certain result is seen at all times.

To anticipate an objection, the text says but if the result, because it is accompanied by a certain specific cooperative cause.
errors.why: The whole passage up to ཕྱིར་རོ is the opponent's objection that 'but if the result' anticipates; the English states it as the author's view and detaches its reason clause.

fix.find:
Even if any particular condition of the wind humor or others were the cause, not every specific instance would possess all forms of desire and so forth. One must infer this because a certain result is seen at all times.

To anticipate an objection, the text says but if the result, because it is accompanied by a certain specific cooperative cause.
fix.replace: Anticipating the objection, "Even if some particular condition of wind and the rest is the cause, not every particular state has all of desire and so forth; this is to be inferred from a definite result being seen at all times, because [the cause] is accompanied by a definite particular cooperating factor," the text says "but if the result."

errors.english: No matter which word it depends on, the meaning is extracted from that cause.
errors.why: A grammatical note: as correlative of the word 'which' (gang), 'from that cause' is to be supplied.

fix.find: No matter which word it depends on, the meaning is extracted from that cause.
fix.replace: As correlative of the word 'which', 'from that cause' is to be supplied.

errors.english: The phrase at that time should be placed before the words because of that cause, depending on which word it relates to
errors.why: 'In that case' (on the alternative reading), 'that cause', correlative of 'which', is placed first; the English turns this into a lemma and misreads 'the word which'.

errors.english: it is connected to the object of observation
errors.why: It is construed with the verb 'is observed' (ཉེ་བར་དམིགས་སོ), not with an 'object of observation'.
'It is not so' rebuts the doubt (the verb འགོག་པ follows on the next side); it does not raise one.

errors.english: the variegated beauty of their commands, which crown their victory
errors.why: The gods bear on their heads the variegated garland of commands of those victorious ones, beautiful with excellent things; 'garland' and 'excellent things' are lost and 'which crown their victory' is not in the text.

errors.english: the cause of the quarrel which is being sustained must also be expelled from the residence
errors.why: It is the monk who furnishes the cause of a quarrel who is to be banished, not the cause itself (as the commentary itself then explains).

fix.find: the cause of the quarrel which is being sustained must also be expelled from the residence
fix.replace: one who furnishes the cause of a quarrel must also be expelled from the residence
